findings.message: D1 applies the contract to the open-ended set “ゲート・検証系タスク（…等）” without recording how that universally quantified scope is resolved. This leaves the migration boundary unbounded as commands evolve. Record one permitted resolution: delegate membership to an existing authority, choose a conservative over-approximation, or acknowledge strict implementation with a depth estimate.

This new command reaches an external process and filesystem boundary with arbitrary OS-native argv and unbounded captured output, while the project’s environment-assumption declaration remains TODO and the spec does not define supported platforms, encoding, resource limits, or failure behavior. Declare these assumptions before exposing this dispatch path.

The regression uses raw source-substring checks (`case `, `if `, and `sed `) to decide whether legacy wrapper logic is absent. This violates `knowledge/conventions/testing.md`’s prohibition on source-substring assertions and is structurally unreliable: harmless description text can fail the test, while differently spelled script logic can pass. Parse `Makefile.toml` as TOML and assert that the task has no `script` field; the new `task_section` heuristic can then be removed.

The three dependency checks preserve only one sentinel gate per newly extracted `*-local-steps` task. T003/OUT-01 requires aggregate task membership to remain unchanged, but dropping any other gate (for example `clippy-local`, `check-layers-local`, or an ADR signal gate) would still pass this regression. Assert each child task’s complete direct dependency set so the migration cannot silently weaken an aggregate gate.

The replacement still determines whether `script` is absent with a hand-written line scan. `task_toml_optional_value` recognizes only the exact textual form `script = `, so valid TOML such as `script=[...]` or a quoted key is reported as absent and the wrapper regression passes incorrectly. This extends the line-based heuristic prohibited by `knowledge/conventions/prefer-type-safe-abstractions.md`; parse the task through a TOML decoder and inspect the resulting field structurally.

The new test unconditionally calls `task_dependency_set` for `ci-local` and `ci-container`, but those wrapper tasks intentionally have no `dependencies` field; their dependencies are on `ci-local-steps`. `task_toml_value` therefore panics with a missing-key error, so this regression test always fails. Restrict the exact dependency assertion to `ci-local-steps` (or inspect the dependency closure for the wrappers).

The compose-wrapper assertion derives `child` from the current `*-local` task via `task_gate_child`, so the test does not independently verify the required mapping. A wrong shared mapping (for example, both `ci` and `ci-local` pointing to the wrong steps task) would be accepted. Use explicit expected child values for `ci-rust`, `ci`, and `ci-track` instead of deriving the oracle from the Makefile.

未宣言の前提への依存: `GateOutputComposition::build` は常に `ProcessGateRunner` を注入しますが、その driver から直接到達する実行経路は `Command::output()` で子プロセスの終了を無期限に待ち、stdout/stderr 全体を無制限にメモリへ保持します。spec に処理時間・出力サイズ・メモリ上限や超過時の動作はなく、`environment-assumptions.md` の資源上限も TODO のため、停止しない／大量出力する子プロセスが CLI を永久にブロックまたは OOM させます。上限と失敗動作を宣言・実装した runner を注入してください。

未宣言の前提への依存: `GateOutputComposition::build` は全 platform で `FsGateLogPersistence` を注入しますが、この adapter の保存経路は Linux の `/proc/self/fd` に依存し、非 Linux では常に `Unsupported` を返します。`environment-assumptions.md` の対応 platform は TODO のままで、spec にも Linux/procfs 必須条件がないため、macOS/Windows や procfs のない Linux では全 gate-output 実行が失敗します。Linux/procfs 制約を正式に宣言するか、対応 platform ごとの安全な adapter を配線してください。
`SpawnFailed` の error を未加工で stdout に埋め込んでいるため、エラー文字列に改行や大量の内容が含まれると、短い理由だけという出力契約を破り、行数・サイズも無制限になります。`truncate_line` 相当の bounded rendering を適用してください。
`GateExitCode` の i32 値を `u8` に変換できない場合、実際の終了コードを常に 1 に置き換えます。256 超の終了コード（特に Windows のプロセス終了コード）では、FAIL 判定自体は維持されても既存の終了コードを保持できず、`render_summary` が表示する値とも不一致になります。境界での終了コード方針を明示・実装してください。

Nested-summary recognition handles the bare `FAIL` verdict but not the project-owned fallback bullets emitted by `render_summary`: `- child exited with status ...` and `- could not start child command: ...`. When an aggregate wraps such a leaf failure, `failure_excerpts` returns only `FAIL`; since the excerpt list is nonempty, the outer renderer also suppresses its own status fallback. The final stdout therefore contains only `- FAIL`, with no failed item or short reason, violating AC-02. Recognize these summary bullet forms and add regressions for fallback and spawn failures.

The documented `cargo make gate-output --name <name> -- <command> [args...]` invocation can pass the `--` separator through `$@`, but this wrapper does not strip it before invoking `bin/sotp`. The child command may therefore be parsed incorrectly; handle the separator as the other shell wrappers do.

The new Makefile task embeds shell control logic (`case ... shift`) to normalize arguments. The briefing explicitly requires Makefile.toml tasks to remain thin wrappers without `case`/`if`/`sed`; move separator handling into `bin/sotp` or otherwise keep this task declarative.

The new `cargo run -p cli` wrappers at lines 205, 212, 219, 226, and 863 trigger `template-export-smoke-local`'s fail-closed scan, so `cargo make ci-local`/container CI will fail unconditionally. Use the supported exported `bin/sotp` gate-output surface or update the guard in the same change.

The migrated CI leaf tasks now execute the workspace-relative `bin/sotp`, but that binary is ignored by both Git and Docker and the `tools` image does not install it. Consequently, fresh-checkout `ci-container` fails before `test-local`/`test-cli-feature-off-local`/`test-doc-local` can run, and `ci-track-container` similarly fails at `test-obligation-check-local`. Provide a current-source `sotp` executable within these CI paths instead of depending on a developer's ignored host binary.

Wrapping `test-nocapture-local` with `gate-output` captures the child's stdout/stderr in the full log and emits only the compact summary, while the public `test-nocapture` task still promises to run tests “with stdout/stderr shown.” Update the public task contract to describe the new behavior (or preserve live output if that promise remains intended).

`ci-local` と `ci-container` の依存一覧を private な `ci-local-steps` へ移したため、`knowledge/adr/2026-06-15-0025-operational-docs-restructure-unified.md#D9` が指定する「両タスクの dependencies を Quality Gates の機械可読 SSoT とする」契約と矛盾する。既存の保守手順や検査が両タスクを読むと空のゲート一覧になるため、依存関係の発見可能な正本を維持するか、明示的な ADR 変更として関連する harness surface を同期する必要がある。

新しい集約 wrapper は、すでに `gate-output` で包まれた `test-local` などを含む `ci-local-steps` をさらに `gate-output` で包む。leaf の失敗抜粋は `- FAIL …` のように再整形される一方、外側の failure classifier はその形式を失敗項目として認識せず、最終サマリには cargo-make の汎用的な exit-code 行しか残らない。このため失敗したテスト項目と短い理由を示すという briefing の AC-02 を満たさない。失敗する leaf を通した集約経路で項目名と理由が最終 stdout に残るよう wiring を修正する必要がある。

`ci-local` and `ci-container` retain the full quality-gate `dependencies` list while also invoking `ci-local-steps`, whose dependencies contain the same gates. Cargo-make therefore executes every gate twice for these aggregate tasks, doubling CI work and potentially repeating side effects. Remove the duplicated dependency path or make the wrapper depend only on the steps task while preserving the required gate-output boundary.

The `env` flag does not make the aggregate dependencies run inside the `gate-output` command: cargo-make executes dependencies before the task command, so these gates emit raw output and a dependency failure prevents the `gate-output` command from running at all. The `condition` guards therefore cannot establish the required aggregate PASS/FAIL summary and log-path contract for either `ci-local` or `ci-container`. The dependency execution must be moved under the wrapped child command, or the wrapper must otherwise capture and summarize dependency failures.

The new leaf conditions do not distinguish aggregate dependency execution from `*-steps` execution: `CARGO_MAKE_TASK` is the leaf task currently being run, so a dependency such as `fmt-check-local` satisfies `env = { CARGO_MAKE_TASK = "fmt-check-local" }` both when invoked from `ci-local`'s restored D9 dependency list and when invoked through `ci-local-steps`. Consequently the aggregate gates still execute every shared leaf twice, defeating the intended de-duplication and doubling CI work. The guard must use a flag propagated specifically to the wrapped child invocation (or remove the duplicate dependency path).

The new leaf conditions do not distinguish aggregate dependency execution from `*-steps` execution: `CARGO_MAKE_TASK` is set to the task currently being executed, so a dependency such as `fmt-check-local` satisfies `env = { CARGO_MAKE_TASK = "fmt-check-local" }` both when invoked from `ci-local`'s restored D9 dependency list and when invoked through `ci-local-steps`. The aggregate gates therefore still execute shared leaves twice, defeating the intended de-duplication and doubling CI work. Use a flag propagated specifically to the wrapped child invocation, or remove the duplicate dependency path.

`knowledge/adr/2026-06-15-0025-operational-docs-restructure-unified.md#D9` は `ci` wrapper が Docker 経由で `ci-local` に委譲すると定めているが、この wrapper は新設の `ci-local-steps` を直接実行している。したがって、文書化された SSoT である `ci-local` / `ci-container` の dependencies だけを保守しても `cargo make ci` の実行対象には反映されず、第三の手動同期リストが実際の gate membership を所有してしまう。外側の `gate-output` は維持したまま、子タスクを `ci-local` に戻す必要がある。

`ci-local` と `ci-container` に復元した dependencies は、cargo-make の仕様上 `gate-output` command より先に実行され、その stdout は wrapper に捕捉されない。成功時でも `test-local` 等の個別 `PASS`/log 行や未包装 verifier の出力が先に流れ、その後に集約 `PASS` が出るため、CN-01/CN-02/AC-01 の「対象タスクの stdout は単一判定とログパスに限り、個別 PASS 行を含まない」を満たさない。二重実行自体は briefing で受け入れ済みだが、最初の実行がサマリ契約を迂回することは受け入れられていないため、D9 の発見可能性と stdout 捕捉を両立する wiring が必要である。

T001 omits the current `cli_driver::render::CommandOutcome` catalogue entry (`action: reference`) from its attributions. Reference entries also require attribution even when the owner makes no change; attribute this entry to T001, where `GateOutputDriver` converges on the existing outcome shape.
`fs::write` の前後で symlink を検査していますが、検査と書き込みが分離しているため、その間にログファイルまたは親ディレクトリを symlink に置換されると trusted root 外へ書き込めます。検査と安全な作成を原子的に行ってください。
ログ名が command name・PID・`SystemTime::as_nanos()` の組み合わせだけで、同一プロセスの並行呼び出しや時計精度の低い環境では衝突し得ます。`fs::write` は既存ファイルを切り詰めるため、別ゲートの完全ログを上書きして AC-03 を破壊します。排他的な一意ファイル作成を使用してください。
`Command::output()` は stdout/stderr 全体を無制限にメモリへ読み込みます。完全ログ保持のための入力サイズ・メモリ上限、超過時の失敗動作が spec または環境前提に宣言されておらず、子プロセスが大量出力するとゲートが OOM または資源枯渇します。ストリーミングまたは明示的な上限を設けてください。

ログファイル作成を Linux 専用の `/proc/self/fd` と `O_NOFOLLOW` に依存させ、`#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]` では常に `Unsupported` を返しています。macOS/Windows 等では `FsGateLogPersistence` が必ず失敗し、環境前提にも対応 platform の宣言がありません。対応 platform を明示するか、各対応 platform の安全な実装を提供してください。

Linux 実装も `/proc` がマウントされていることを前提に `/proc/self/fd/<fd>` 経由でログを作成しています。procfs が利用できない Linux 環境では全ログ永続化が失敗しますが、この OS/filesystem 前提は spec または環境宣言に記録されていません。前提を宣言するか、procfs に依存しない安全な descriptor-relative 実装を用意してください。

`fs::create_dir_all(&log_directory)` は descriptor-relative な安全な directory walk より前に実行され、`check_path` 後の race で `tmp` または `gate` を symlink に置換されると、trusted root 外にディレクトリを作成します。後段の `open_log_directory` が安全でも、この外部作成は既に発生しています。ディレクトリ作成も descriptor-relative な処理に統一し、path-based `create_dir_all` を削除してください。

`check_trusted_root()` の symlink 検査後に `trusted_root.canonicalize()` を実行しており、検査と canonicalize の間に root component を symlink へ置換されると、その symlink の指す外部ディレクトリを新たな trusted root として descriptor walk します。同様に non-Unix の `canonical_log_directory` も race 後の解決先を信頼します。入力 root を path-based canonicalize せず、検査済み descriptor から相対的に処理して fail closed にしてください。

`output.status.code().map_or(1, ...)` collapses abnormal child termination (for example, SIGINT/SIGTERM on Unix, where `code()` is `None`) into the ordinary exit code 1. This violates the required child-status preservation and loses interrupt/signal semantics even though the child did run. Represent abnormal termination explicitly across the port, or apply a documented status mapping, and add a signal-termination regression test.

`status.code() == None` represents distinct abnormal terminations (for example SIGINT versus SIGTERM on Unix), but this adapter collapses all of them into the invented `-1` exit code. The downstream boundary then converts that value to generic code 1, so the child status and interrupt semantics required by the briefing are still not preserved; the new test only codifies the lossy mapping. Carry normal exit and signal termination as distinct typed outcomes (including the signal value), and map them only at the process exit boundary.

`GateProcessPort`'s contract fulfillment—and its CN-03 voluntary binding later in this file—uses only `test_gate_process_port_returns_complete_output_and_preserves_exit_judgment`, which invokes a test-only `StubRunner` preloaded with the exact asserted output. This is not evidence that the production process boundary preserves child exit status, so it substitutes a usecase double for layer-owned runtime behavior and overclaims the edge. Bind these records to the `ProcessGateRunner` infrastructure tests or a shared contract suite exercised against that adapter.

The updated `GateProcessPort` fulfillment and CN-03 voluntary binding have not been re-evaluated. `test-obligation results` reports two stale done-state verdicts, and `bin/sotp test-obligation check` exits 1 with `TestChanged` drift for AC-04 and CN-03; the cache still cites the previous usecase `StubRunner` tests. The host must rerun semantic evaluation so these infrastructure bindings receive fresh verdicts before the gate can be considered green.

New failure formats can therefore disappear from the AC-02 excerpt. Record one of the permitted open-set resolutions.

`cli::commands::gate_output::execute` restates the upstream logging, summary-output, and exit-code behavior in `docs`. Keep only the symbol’s operation and anchor citations, per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`GateNameArg::new` returns `Result<Self, GateOutputError>`, but only `InvalidName` is constructible from this operation; `EmptyCommand`, `Clock`, `CreateLogDirectory`, and `Spawn` are unreachable. The entry provides no producible-subset or breadth justification.

`cli::commands::gate_output::prepare_log_path` can only produce `Clock` or `CreateLogDirectory` because it receives an already validated `GateNameArg`, yet returns the five-variant `GateOutputError` without documenting or justifying the unreachable variants.

`cli::commands::gate_output::run_child` can only produce `EmptyCommand` or `Spawn`, yet returns the five-variant `GateOutputError` without documenting or justifying the unreachable `InvalidName`, `Clock`, and `CreateLogDirectory` variants.

`cli::commands::gate_output::render_summary` models the three execution states with independent `exit_code: ChildExitCode` and `spawn_reason: Option<&str>` parameters. This admits contradictory values such as a successful exit code with a spawn-failure reason, which the renderer silently ignores. Replace the pair—ideally together with the associated output—with a dedicated completed/child-failed/spawn-failed outcome enum so invalid combinations are unrepresentable.

`GateRunOutcome::ChildFailed` accepts an unrestricted `ChildExitCode`, while `ChildExitCode::from_status` can construct the success code. The catalogue therefore still admits `ChildFailed { exit_code: 0, ... }`, contradicting the variant and its claimed closed outcome shape. Use a single `ChildExited { exit_code, output }` variant and classify success when rendering, or introduce a validated non-success exit-code type.

The `ChildExitCode::from_status` and `ChildExitCode::failure` method declarations use `Self` as their return type. The types checklist requires concrete type names; declare both returns as `ChildExitCode`.

`GateNameArg::new(String) -> GateNameArg` accepts every opaque CLI label, while `cli::commands::gate_output::prepare_log_path` declares no containment validation or encoding and `PrepareLogPathError` can report only clock/directory failures. Consequently no entry owns the fail-closed `tmp/gate/` boundary: a label containing `../` or an absolute-path prefix can escape the required directory. Assign exactly one owner by validating construction or safely encoding/rejecting labels during path preparation.

`cli::commands::gate_output::execute`, `run_child`, `prepare_log_path`, and `render_summary` are declared as `FreeFunction`s in the `cli` process-entrypoint layer, but their contracts respectively own application orchestration, process/filesystem adapter operations, and result rendering. This contradicts the thin-bin contract in `type-designer-kind-selection.md` and `tddd-product-correctness.md`: `cli` should parse, dispatch, and convert the final exit code, while orchestration, secondary I/O adapters, and invoke/render belong in their corresponding usecase, infrastructure, and cli_driver layers.

`cli::commands::gate_output::prepare_log_path` claims exclusive ownership of containment beneath `tmp/gate`, but it accepts no trusted root, returns an unrestricted `PathBuf`, and `PrepareLogPathError` can report only clock or directory-creation failures. It therefore cannot reject a symlinked `tmp`/`tmp/gate` component or preserve the guarantee across the later write, so the declared fail-closed owner cannot construct its required rejection data. The contract needs a persistence boundary that owns the actual write and represents outside-root/symlink rejection explicitly.

`GateLogPersistencePort::persist`, `GateProcessPort::run`, and the I/O-orchestrating `GateRunService::execute` are all declared synchronous (`is_async: false`), but none of their entry docs acknowledges or justifies the blocking process/filesystem boundary. Either make the ports async or record the deliberate bounded, single-shot CLI synchronization choice so adapter color is explicit.

`GateAdapterFailureReason` is classified as a usecase `ValueObject`, but its docs explicitly describe unconstrained adapter diagnostic text to which the application assigns no domain meaning. That establishes neither invariant ownership nor semantics independent of adapter/workflow concerns; model this transport value as a DTO (or keep a documented opaque `String`) rather than stretching `ValueObject`.

`GateLogPersistenceError::Clock` exposes `std::time::SystemTimeError` from the runtime adapter through the usecase API. This violates the declared boundary contract that adapter failures cross as `GateAdapterFailureReason` and leaks a runtime-specific error type to callers. Map the clock failure to a usecase-owned reason/value instead.

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: `GateExitCode` assumes every child termination has an `i32` exit code, but processes can terminate without one—for example, via a Unix signal. Neither the spec nor the still-TODO environment declaration defines supported platforms or abnormal-termination mapping, so adapters must invent a value and cannot preserve the original status. Model termination explicitly or declare and enforce the platform/mapping contract.

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: The process boundary requires complete stdout/stderr to be materialized in an unbounded `Vec<u8>` and provides no timeout or cancellation contract. The spec requires a complete persisted log but declares no memory, output-size, or execution-time limits, while the environment declaration remains TODO; a noisy or hung gate can therefore exhaust memory or block indefinitely before persistence. Use streaming/bounded capture with explicit timeout behavior, or declare and enforce the relevant limits.

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: `GateLogPersistencePort::persist` receives no timestamp or clock dependency even though persistence can return `GateLogPersistenceError::Clock`; the runtime adapter must therefore obtain the current time behind this abstraction. This is distinct from the accepted `SystemTimeError` payload deviation: execution time is still required to enter through an explicit usecase-owned clock port, and no clock semantics are declared in the spec or environment assumptions. Inject a clock/timestamp explicitly into the orchestration contract.
